articles.title: Biden says prostate cancer treatment ‘worked as intended’
articles.summary: Former President Biden on Tuesday said the radiation treatment he received for his prostate cancer diagnosis “worked as intended.” Biden shared a lengthy statement on the social platform X acknowledging September as Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, which he said was “more personal for” him this year. The former president’s office revealed in May 2025 that…
articles.body:
Former President Biden on Tuesday said the radiation treatment he received for his prostate cancer diagnosis “worked as intended.”

Biden shared a lengthy statement on the social platform X acknowledging September as Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, which he said was “more personal for” him this year. The former president’s office revealed in May 2025 that he was diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer with bone metastasis, though doctors said his cancer was “hormone-sensitive.” He completed his treatment in October.

“I am deeply grateful to the doctors, nurses and other medical professionals who helped to control my cancer and who continue to take such good care of me,” Biden said in the post. “Their skill, dedication, and compassion mean so much. The radiation treatment from last fall worked as intended, and I continue to do the things I care about, like finishing my memoir.”

His memoir, “ Promise Me, America ,” which will cover his administration’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic and his decision to stop his attempt at a second term in 2024, is slated to release on Nov. 17.

The former president used his statement to thank supporters who have reached out and for keeping “me and my family in your prayers.”

“It’s my hope and prayer that by sharing our experience and being part of this important conversation, we can help save lives,” he continued. “Talk to your doctors. Ask the hard questions. Do it for yourself, and do it for the people who love you.”

His son Hunter Biden told BBC’s “Newsnight” last month that his father’s cancer had spread to other parts of his body, calling it “very debilitating.” Former first lady Jill Biden called her husband’s diagnosis “shocking” and said White House physicians “somehow” missed detecting his cancer.

The former president has kept a low profile since departing the White House last year, though he has opined on President Trump’s actions on occasion. In June, he called Trump “a loser” over his renovation projects across Washington, including the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and the Kennedy Center.

He is expected to join former Presidents Obama, Clinton and George W. Bush at a ceremony at New York City’s Ground Zero to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks. Trump will attend a separate ceremony at the Pentagon.

articles.title: Trump's unusual role at midterm convention revealed as schedule goes public
articles.summary: Trump headlines both nights of the RNC's first-ever GOP midterm convention in Dallas, with JD Vance delivering the Thursday keynote speech.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE — DALLAS — With an eye toward energizing the GOP's MAGA base, the Republican National Committee (RNC) on Tuesday announced the speaking order and times of this week's first-ever GOP midterm convention, and President Donald Trump will be the Primetime headliner both nights. According to the list, which was shared first with Fox News Digital on the eve of the convention, the president will deliver Wednesday's keynote address, which is tentatively scheduled to start at 9 p.m. ET. Trump will return on Thursday evening at the American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas to close out the convention, with remarks after Vice President JD Vance gives the second night's keynote speech. With less than two months to go until the midterm elections, Trump and Republicans are gathering in Texas for their historic confab as they aim to energize the party's base ahead of key races that will determine whether the GOP keeps control of Congress. Supporters of the president traditionally do not turn out in robust numbers when Trump is not on the ballot. DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB Democrats and Republicans traditionally hold large nominating conventions during presidential election years. But Trump last year floated the idea of a similar gathering ahead of the midterms to showcase the signature policy achievements he and Republicans in Congress have produced over the past two years. The president called the convention "a truly Historic Event" and "a RALLY like none other!" when he announced it earlier this summer. The convention comes as Republicans face energized Democrats and stiff political headwinds as they defend their slim House and Senate majorities in the midterms. But Republicans are expected to paint a contrast, as they use the convention to spotlight the Democrats' leftward lurch and tie the entire Democratic Party to far-left and socialist proposals. "The midterm election is about the future of our country. President Donald Trump and Republicans are fighting to launch the golden age of America while extreme liberal Democrats want to tear this country apart and create a liberal failed state with their out-of-touch and anti-American views," RNC chair Joe Gruters argued in a statement to Fox News Digital. THESE 12 MIDTERM RACES WILL DECIDE WHICH PARTY CONTROLS THE SENATE Gruters emphasized that "the choice is clear in November and the American people will reject these liberal policies and deliver historic wins for Republicans across the country." The DNC, which remains in debt and decided against holding a similar convention, sees the GOP confab as a chance to blast Republicans. "While everyday Americans struggle to pay their bills, fill up their tanks, or put food on the table, Republicans are hosting a multi-million dollar celebration to satisfy an aging and erratic Trump and tie vulnerable Republican candidates closer to his failed agenda,"," DNC Rapid Response Director Kendall Witmer charged. Witmer argued that "Americans don’t want a ‘Trumpapalooza’ — they want lower costs and affordable healthcare." The convention will also serve as the GOP's closing argument heading into November. In the fight for the Senate majority, Republican candidates in some of the most crucial races will also address the convention. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the GOP nominee in Texas who is facing off against Democratic state Rep. James Talarico in the race to replace Republican Sen. John Cornyn, will speak on the first evening. So will former RNC Chair Mike Whatley, who is defending retiring GOP Sen. Thom Tillis' seat in battleground North Carolina. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER Sen. Jon Husted of Ohio, who is in a pitched fight with former longtime Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown, will also address the crowd, as will Rep. Mike Collins of Georgia, the Republican challenger taking on Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff in swing state Georgia. Former Rep. Mike Rogers of Michigan, who is hoping to flip a Democrat-held open seat in the key Great Lakes battleground as he runs against far-left Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed, speaks on Thursday evening. In the battle for the House, where the GOP holds a razor-thin majority, incumbents and candidates in competitive races will also be in the speaking spotlight. They include Reps. Monica De La Cruz of Texas, Derrick Van Orden of Wisconsin, Rob Bresnahan of Pennsylvania, and candidates Mike LiPetri of New York and Jay Feely of Arizona on Wednesday night. Among the House Republican incumbents and candidates in close races speaking on Thursday are Reps. Ryan Mackenzie of Pennsylvania and Mike Lawler of New York, along with nominees Greg Cunningham of New Mexico, Derrick Merrin of Ohio and Eric Flores of Texas. STATE OF PLAY: WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN IN THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS Speaker Mike Johnson will speak on Thursday evening, according to the RNC schedule. Johnson's Senate counterpart, Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-South Dakota), is notably absent from the list of speakers released by the RNC. But a source familiar with the planning tells Fox News Digital that Thune will be in Dallas, with a full schedule that includes helping Senate candidates fundraise. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who is running for a fourth term leading the Lone Star State, speaks on Thursday. So does Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas, the conservative firebrand who is not on the ballot this year but could make a second White House bid in 2028. Meanwhile, some of the biggest names in Trump's Cabinet are scheduled to speak, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Wednesday evening, and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who spearheaded the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement, on Thursday evening.

articles.title: 'The View' co-host demands 25th Amendment be used against Trump, suggests Cabinet could do it after midterms
articles.summary: Sunny Hostin raised invoking the 25th Amendment against President Donald Trump on "The View," speculating the Cabinet could act if Republicans lose the House and Senate.
articles.body: "The View" co-host Sunny Hostin raised using the 25th Amendment against President Donald Trump on Tuesday, as the ABC talk show returned from its summer break. "My question is when do we really start, in earnest — and I mean this honestly — considering the 25th Amendment," Hostin said. "I think when the Republicans lose the House, and they lose the Senate, they’re going to want to have some control over this person, this person that is in the office, and JD Vance would then be that replacement and I wonder if the Cabinet then looks at each other and says, ‘OK, we’ve got to take control of this, 25th Amendment,’" she added. The 25th Amendment to the Constitution empowers a president’s Cabinet to remove him from office if he is unable to do the job. PUSH TO OUST TRUMP EXPOSES CRACKS AMONG DEMOCRATS ON STRATEGY, TIMING Co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin pushed back, saying she didn't think Trump's Cabinet would ever take such action. "I think if they didn’t do it after January 6, in that period before he left office [in 2021], it’s never going to happen," she said. "It is rich for ‘The View’ to talk about cognitive abilities when they themselves suffer from a mental illness: Trump Derangement Syndrome," RNC Deputy Communications Director Delanie Bomar told Fox News Digital. "President Trump is mentally fit, sound, and sharp — something the hosts of ‘The View’ can’t say they are." Co-hosts Whoopi Goldberg and Joy Behar have also called for the use of the 25th Amendment against Trump since he returned to office last year. JEN PSAKI SHUTS DOWN 25TH AMENDMENT TALK ABOUT TRUMP, DECLARES IT'S 'NOT GOING TO HAPPEN' While criticizing Trump's efforts to resolve the war between Russia and Ukraine in September 2025, Goldberg said, "He had an opportunity to do so much more than he offered them, and they don’t consider him to be serious anymore, and I’m worried. What is the amendment, the 20-" The co-hosts took their guesses at which amendment Goldberg was referencing, making multiple attempts before Hostin eventually informed them that it was the 25th Amendment. "They questioned Biden’s competence," Goldberg said at the time. "If Biden had acted like this, I would have said take him and sit him down somewhere, but this was not — this was not presidential, and this was not helpful." After Trump unveiled plaques beneath portraits of his predecessors, including Barack Obama and Joe Biden, on the new White House Presidential Walk of Fame in December 2025, Behar asked when the Cabinet would push to remove the president. "When are they going to invoke the 25th Amendment? Does he have to run naked into the White House or what? What is that amendment for if not for this?" Behar said, drawing laughter from the audience. FCC CHAIR MOCKS 'THE VIEW' HOST SUNNY HOSTIN FOR BLATANT PARTISANSHIP AS SHE PLEADS FOR DEMS TO WIN SENATE "The View" launched a campaign seeking public support in June amid a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) investigation into the liberal talk show as the agency cracks down on equal time for political candidates after Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico joined the co-hosts for an interview. Tell the FCC to let the viewers decide."

articles.title: Fetterman leans on unlikely GOP ally as Dems sharpen their knives over explosive report
articles.summary: Senate Democrat John Fetterman calls leaked staff texts about skipping constituent meetings "smears" as Dave McCormick defends him on social media.
articles.body: Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., is under fire over leaked texts with his staff in which he brushed off meetings with a children’s hospital and paralyzed veterans, but he is pushing back, calling the reports "smears" with support from his Republican Pennsylvania colleague, Sen. Dave McCormick. Fetterman broke his silence following a bombshell report based on leaked text messages between him and his staff that portrayed him as brushing off basic duties of being a senator, including meetings with constituents. Fetterman told CNN in a statement that "disgruntled" staffers had concocted the story, first reported by the Wall Street Journal, to knock his reputation. FETTERMAN FACES DEM REVOLT AS BOMBSHELL REPORT FUELS PUSH TO OUST HIM: 'DISGRACE' "Per usual — lies, half-truths, innuendos, smears and anonymous," Fetterman said. "No matter how many smears or stories, I’m proud to continue to deliver for Pennsylvania," he continued. The lawmaker’s response follows an explosive report published last week that painted Fetterman as a politician more interested in appearing on Fox News to discuss Israel than meeting with constituents, including a group of paralyzed veterans from his state, and opting to blow off a funeral for slain police officers because it would have taken too long. While other Democratic members of the Pennsylvania delegation were furious with Fetterman, his fellow senator, McCormick, came to his defense. "These stories are the latest example of outrageously disloyal staff and forces on the Left using anonymous leaks to cancel my friend John Fetterman," McCormick said on X. "They hate that he is an independent thinker who refuses to fall into line so they want to silence him." WHY TRUMP, GOP ARE COURTING JOHN FETTERMAN, WHO INSISTS HE’LL REMAIN A DEMOCRAT Fetterman and McCormick share a unique relationship in a Congress that has grown increasingly partisan. They’re one of three Senate duos from a purple state, and Fetterman has vowed to not support an opponent when and if McCormick runs for re-election in 2030. "Well, I would absolutely never move against my friend," Fetterman told reporters. They also launched a joint fundraising effort in July, called Common Ground PA, according to federal financial filings. DNC VICE CHAIR ATTACKS DEMOCRATIC SEN. JOHN FETTERMAN: 'YOU’RE A MESS' And the pair spent Labor Day together, per a post from McCormick, where they toured Bell & Evans, a chicken processing company in Pennsylvania. "He and I will continue to work together to deliver for Pennsylvania by saving jobs at US Steel, passing a new law to make housing more affordable, securing $600 million to replace the Delaware River Bridge, and delivering critical funding to protect Presque Isle State Park," McCormick continued. Still, members of the Pennsylvania delegation and beyond, including the vice chair of the Democratic National Committee, are laying the groundwork to oust him. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Rep. Chris Deluzio, D-Pa., a progressive representing southwest Pennsylvania, charged that Fetterman’s behavior was "pathetic," and said that "this man has no sense of duty." Whether Fetterman mount a bid for re-election in 2028 remains to be seen. "He is not up for the high office he was elected to — and we in Pennsylvania will do something about it in 2028," Deluzio said on X.

articles.title: National Guard member arrested in DC, accused of pulling gun in argument over hairstyles
articles.summary: A National Guard member was arrested last week, accused of pointing a gun at a fellow guard member in late August, an arrest affidavit shows. Zion Mitchell, 21, of Georgia, is facing felony charges of assault with a dangerous weapon and possession of a firearm while committing a crime of violence or dangerous crime, according…
articles.body:
A National Guard member was arrested last week, accused of pointing a gun at a fellow guard member in late August, an arrest affidavit shows.

Zion Mitchell, 21, of Georgia, is facing felony charges of assault with a dangerous weapon and possession of a firearm while committing a crime of violence or dangerous crime, according to the affidavit filed in District of Columbia Superior Court.

As of Friday, Mitchell was being held without bond because of “the nature of the crimes,” according to the court docket.

On Aug. 25, Mitchell and a group of National Guard members were on break from patrol and were sitting inside a black van in front of a Popeyes on H Street NE, the affidavit states.

During an argument with another guard member over whether their hairstyles followed Army regulations, Mitchell told her that he would “slap the Jackson 5 out of you,” with the ensuing back-and-forth leading to the woman telling Mitchell, “Shut the f‑‑‑ up. Try me,” per the affidavit.

At that point, the woman heard a “holster click,” with one witness saying, “Put that up. You almost shot me in the hand.” The woman was informed later that Mitchell had drawn his weapon.

The woman told investigators she believed Mitchell’s weapon was loaded, as all firearms held by National Guard members were. One witness told investigators that Mitchell said the gun “was on safe,” while another confirmed his gun was loaded and had a round in the chamber.

In addition to Mitchell and the woman, six National Guard members were in the van at the time. Several of them corroborated to investigators that Mitchell pointed his weapon at the woman.

During his interview with detectives, Mitchell initially said he was in a “playful argument” with the woman when he pulled a magazine out of his vest and pointed a pistol at her, adding it was part of the “playful banter,” the affidavit states.

The 21-year-old later recanted, saying he pointed the pistol “in the direction” of the woman but at a roughly 45-degree angle and not toward her head.

One witness, a woman, told investigators the alleged victim told her that Mitchell “threatens” women and did not get along with him after she rejected his advances.

National Guard troops have been in D.C. for more than a year as part of President Trump’s intention to crack down on crime in the nation’s capital.

As of Monday, more than 3,100 guard members from 17 Republican-led states, D.C., Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands were in the capital, according to data from Joint Task Force D.C.

The Pentagon is planning to maintain a National Guard presence in D.C. through the end of Trump’s second term in January 2029, a guard official told The Hill in March.

articles.title: PMO denies that UAE warned Netanyahu about October 7, Abu Dhabi refuses to comment
articles.summary: Abu Dhabi says it will not join Israel’s political debate after a report claimed Mohammed bin Zayed warned Netanyahu before October 7. The Prime Minister’s O...
articles.body:
Abu Dhabi denies warning Israel about Hamas attack before October 7, stating that if any relevant information was shared, it was done through intelligence channels between the two countries.

Dispute arises over credibility of report, with one side arguing that Haaretz would not publish such a claim without verifying sources, while the other side questions the lack of documentation or records to support the alleged warning from the UAE.

Abu Dhabi says it will not join Israel's political debate after a report claimed Mohammed bin Zayed warned Netanyahu before October 7.

The Prime Minister's Office on Tuesday strongly denied the Haaretz report, which alleged that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was warned by the United Arab Emirates about Hamas's October 7 attack, writing that the "press reports are false."

"No warning was given to the Prime Minister from the United Arab Emirates before October 7th. If there was any relevant information, it was passed through intelligence channels between the two countries," the PMO stated.

The UAE Foreign Ministry also published a statement on the report, saying it refuses to comment on "speculation" about whether the two countries spoke. Notably, however, the UAE did not confirm or deny the Haaretz report .

"UAE and Israeli government entities have maintained open and direct lines of communication since the inception of the relationship more than five years ago. When necessary, all relevant intelligence has been and continues to be communicated between the relevant entities."

UAE officials also indicated that, from their perspective, it is not their role to issue a denial in response to every media report published in Israel. The message conveyed was that the UAE does not interfere in Israeli elections and will not serve as the government's "public relations office."

In a conversation with Ben Caspit on 103FM on Tuesday, Yinon Magal presented the prime minister's denial and said Netanyahu maintained that no such conversation had taken place.

Magal said that if such an event had indeed occurred, it could also be verified with the head of the National Security Council and other officials who would have been expected to know about the conversation.

Caspit, by contrast, said he was convinced that the report was credible. He said former prime minister Naftali Bennett, who is close to bin Zayed, had confirmed the account, and argued that the fact that officials in Abu Dhabi had not rushed to deny the report further strengthened its credibility in his view.

"The Emirates is a tremendous ally of ours. If he remains silent, as far as I'm concerned, that is also a statement," Caspit said.

Caspit also linked the report to earlier warnings from Egypt before the attack.

"This joins the Egyptian warning that was published in a million places," he said, arguing that as more reports accumulated, they strengthened the picture, in his view, that actors outside Israel had warned of an unusual move by Hamas.

"The 'why didn't they wake him up' campaign is now becoming the question, 'why didn't he wake us up?'" Caspit said.

Dispute continues over credibility of report

Caspit added that, in his assessment, Haaretz would not have published such a claim without cross-checking sources. He called for waiting to hear from former CIA director William Burns, who, according to the report, was also involved in warnings from bin Zayed.

Magal, however, rejected that argument, saying that if such a conversation had indeed taken place, there would have been documentation and records of it. Therefore, he said, it was difficult to believe that Netanyahu would issue such a sweeping denial.

"If there had been a conversation, the prime minister would not say there wasn't one, because there are records. Someone would already have leaked that it happened," Magal said.

Caspit again argued that the report fit, in his view, into a series of warnings and pieces of information that had accumulated before the attack. He added that the central question was now not only what the security agencies knew on the night between October 6 and 7, but also what warnings reached the political leadership in the weeks beforehand and what was done with them.

Recent reports have examined additional claims about warnings received before October 7, including accounts of Naftali Bennett confirming the UAE warning report and earlier reports of warnings from Israeli security officials.

The dispute between the two ended without agreement. Magal demanded evidence that the conversation with bin Zayed had in fact taken place, while Caspit argued that the collection of reports and sources strengthened the credibility of the report in his view.
authors: ANNA BARSKY AND JERUSALEM POST STAFF

articles.title: Hochul voices support for Mamdani after Giuliani tells him to skip 9/11 ceremony
articles.summary: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) on Tuesday voiced support for New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) after one of his predecessors, former Mayor Rudy Giuliani (R), criticized him for planning to attend the city’s 25th anniversary commemoration of the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks. “Division should not prevail over the spirit of unity…
articles.body:
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) on Tuesday voiced support for New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) after one of his predecessors, former Mayor Rudy Giuliani (R), criticized him for planning to attend the city’s 25th anniversary commemoration of the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks.

“Division should not prevail over the spirit of unity that brought us together after September 11th,” Hochul said in a post on the social platform X . “On this 25th anniversary, we should honor those we lost by coming together again as New Yorkers and Americans. The Mayor of New York City will be there, as he should be.”

The calls from Giuliani and others urging Mamdani to skip the ceremony stem in part from the mayor’s appointment of Ramzi Kassem, who previously represented a convicted al-Qaeda member whose brother-in-law was among the 19 hijackers who perpetrated the Sept. 11 attack, as the city’s top legal counsel.

The move led some families of 9/11 victims to launch a petition urging Mamdani not to go. The petition claims Mamdani supports people perceived as “dismissive of American institutions or insufficiently critical of extremist ideologies.”

Giuliani, who led New York City when the attacks took place, has touted conspiracy theories tinged with anti-Muslim sentiment about Mamdani in connection with the attacks and said it offended him that the mayor will attend.

Mamdani has dismissed these claims and conspiracy theories, saying the focus leading up to Friday’s commemoration should be about the families of those killed 25 years ago “in the horrific act of terror on Sept. 11,” the mayor told reporters Monday.

“And a focus also on the first responders who gave everything they could to this city and to the people who came together to try and help their fellow New Yorkers,” Mamdani added. “And so, in the days to come, my focus will be on attending events that memorialize that incredible courage and I will be there on Friday at the memorial just as I was last year.”

Mamdani said he “did not have much more to add” when asked about Giuliani’s comments.

Alongside the Empire State’s governor and the Big Apple’s mayor, four of the five living presidents, along with Vice President Vance, are expected to attend the Ground Zero ceremony.

President Trump, born in the city’s Queens borough, will not attend Ground Zero, instead choosing to speak at the Pentagon for a separate commemoration, as the Pentagon was also struck during the Sept. 11 attacks. It will be the second year in which he has done so from Washington, though he and Vance attended the Ground Zero ceremony in 2024.

articles.title: Mamdani drops massive 9/11 records trove as old claims about Ground Zero come under fire
articles.summary: Over 170,000 pages released by Mayor Zohran Mamdani reveal internal memos questioning whether Ground Zero air was safe after the 9/11 attacks.
articles.body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani released more than 170,000 pages of records Tuesday that call into question public claims that the air around Ground Zero was safe to breathe following the 9/11 attacks. Mamdani's office released an initial trove of approximately 170,000 pages of records, including documents found in 68 boxes at the Department of Environmental Protection in 2025 that date back to the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks. The records release comes just days before the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks in which 2,977 people were killed. Thousands of people exposed to the toxic dust and debris after 9/11 have since died from illnesses associated with the attacks, while many more continue to suffer from health conditions, according to the World Trade Center Health Program and other health authorities. AMERICA’S HEARTLAND COMES FACE-TO-FACE WITH 9/11 HISTORY AS 25TH ANNIVERSARY NEARS Then-EPA Administrator Christine Todd Whitman said in a Sept. 18, 2001, press release that monitoring results indicated the air near the World Trade Center was safe to breathe, following EPA assurances about environmental hazards dating to Sept. 13. "People got sick because the leaders they trusted lied and told them they were safe to breathe in toxic air," Mamdani shared during a Tuesday press conference. The documents revealed that ten months after the terrorist attacks, traces of asbestos were found on the roof of a building located at 15 John Street, less than a mile from where the World Trade Center once stood. The records show that asbestos was detected at some locations at levels below applicable cleanup or exposure benchmarks and at others at levels that appeared to exceed them; health authorities have said there is no known safe level of asbestos exposure. Among the approximately 170,000 pages released through the online portal is a Feb. 28, 2002, memo from then-Mayor Michael Bloomberg's senior policy adviser, summarizing Rep. Jerrold Nadler's concerns about indoor air quality in Lower Manhattan and warning that the city could face public-relations and legal problems over the cleanup. The memo laid out Nadler's concerns that the Environmental Protection Agency had "handed over responsibility for measuring indoor air quality to the City" without putting in place oversight measures. The memo said the city had passed responsibility for indoor monitoring to property owners and noted that the Health Department had instructed residents to clean buildings with wet mops and rags. "If Nadler’s concerns are justified, we are not Informing people of the real health risks In lower Manhattan, the City may face major public relations problems and Is leaving Itself open to a barrage of lawsuits," the memo, dated Feb. 28, 2002, stated. "At the least we should discontinue telling people to clean their apartments with wet mops and rags. We should be asking FEMA for funds to support Indoor cleanup." articles.body:
New Hampshire Democratic Party Vice Chair Maura Sullivan and former Portsmouth City Council member Stefany Shaheen are facing off for their party’s nod in the primary for the House seat left open by Rep. Chris Pappas (D).

Sullivan holds a narrow lead of Stefany Shaheen, the daughter of retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), in recent polling . Pappas is running for Jeanne Shaheen’s Senate seat.

Stefany Shaheen and Sullivan have locked horns over outside spending and the former’s last name on the campaign trail. Seven other candidates will also run on the Democratic ballot, including progressive Carleigh Beriont.

On the other side of the aisle, car dealership owner Anthony DiLorenzo is duking it out against former state Republican Party Vice Chair Hollie Noveletsky for the GOP nomination. DiLorenzo is endorsed by President Trump.

Polls close at 7 and 8 p.m. EDT. Follow Decision Desk HQ’s live results below.

Pappas faces four other challengers, most notably medical scientist Karishma Manzur. She is running to the House Democrat’s left.

Sununu, meanwhile, is duking it out against seven other Republicans. His main opponent is former Sen. Scott Brown, who represented Massachusetts from 2010-13. Sununu is backed by President Trump and served as the Granite State’s senator from 2003-09.
